title: Image build/sign/release pipeline does not restrict the ref to main's ancestry, letting any pushed tag or dispatched branch become the repo-signed :1 image
impact: A commit that was never merged to the protected `main` branch is published to GHCR as `:1`, `:<version>`, and `:sha-<sha>`, cosign-signed with the repository's keyless OIDC identity, and cut as a GitHub Release. The signature satisfies the exact `cosign verify ...:1 --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/AG-Studio-Apps/stackguard/' ...` command the README instructs users to run, so anyone pulling `:1` directly (per README) or auditing by cosign identity accepts attacker code that has full engine-socket (host) access on deploy. This bypasses the documented release-authorization control ('main is protected; releases are tagged from main after merge').
description: The untrusted source is the ref that triggers publish.yml (any pushed v* tag or any workflow_dispatch branch); the dangerous sinks it reaches without an authorization check are the registry push (line 62), the keyless cosign signing (line 71), and the GitHub Release (line 88). Unlike publish-ios-channel.yml (which gates on `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$TAG_SHA" origin/main`, line 57), publish.yml never verifies the built commit is on the protected main branch.
exploit_scenario: A collaborator with write-but-not-release-manager access (or a leaked CI token) pushes a tag `v9.0.0` pointing at a feature branch containing a backdoored agent, or dispatches publish.yml on that branch. publish.yml checks out and builds that commit, pushes it as `ghcr.io/ag-studio-apps/stackguard:9`/`:9.0.0`, and runs `cosign sign` over its digest with the repo's OIDC identity. A user following the README then pulls and cosign-verifies the tag, sees a valid repository signature, and runs the backdoored image against a Docker/Podman socket.
preconditions: Attacker holds repository write (push) access, or controls a CI credential/action with contents+id-token+packages scope on this repo (fork PRs cannot reach this: no pull_request trigger and forks get no id-token).
No tag-protection ruleset covers `v*` (GitHub's default), so `main`'s branch protection does not extend to tags — a `v*` tag can point at any commit.
For the workflow_dispatch vector, the actor selects an arbitrary branch to run on; checkout+`context: .` builds that branch's HEAD while `git describe` supplies the major tag.
recommendation: Before build/push/sign, add the same authorization gate publish-ios-channel.yml uses, e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main || { echo '::error::ref is not on main'; exit 1; }`, and reject a manual dispatch whose HEAD is not on main's ancestry. Additionally configure a GitHub tag-protection ruleset for `v*` and/or a protected `release` deployment environment so only authorized principals can run the signing job.
